claims.text: Conventionally processed nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 contains nucleation sites for irradiation-induced Cr/V-rich precipitates.
SLM at approximately 300 W and 500–600 mm/s produces rapid solidification in W38Ta36Cr15V11.
The proposed SLM route followed by annealing at approximately 700 °C for 15 minutes produces a non-equilibrium, supersaturated, single-phase BCC nanocrystalline structure.
The SLM route refines the grain structure of W38Ta36Cr15V11.
Rapid solidification limits solute diffusion during fabrication.
Rapid solidification limits the formation of nucleation sites for Cr/V clustering.
A 700 °C, 15-minute post-SLM anneal relieves residual stress.
The brief post-SLM anneal does not induce significant grain growth.
The brief post-SLM anneal does not induce significant re-precipitation.
The proposed processing route maintains a uniform distribution of Cr and V.
A uniform Cr and V distribution minimizes the driving force for radiation-induced precipitation.
The SLM-derived microstructure suppresses radiation-induced Cr/V-rich precipitation during energetic-particle irradiation to approximately 8 dpa below 400 °C.
At approximately 8 dpa below 400 °C, the SLM-processed alloy will have about 50% less Cr/V-rich precipitate volume fraction than the conventionally processed alloy.
Irradiation hardening of the SLM-processed alloy will remain negligible at approximately 8 dpa below 400 °C.
Conventionally processed nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 exhibits measurable Cr/V-rich precipitation after similar irradiation to approximately 8 dpa below 400 °C.
Conventionally processed nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 exhibits no irradiation-hardening change under the stated irradiation conditions.
Residual stresses and microstructural inhomogeneities generated by SLM may alter irradiation-defect distributions and precipitation kinetics.
